displayName: AD Visibility 1a - GPO changed by non-GPO admin
description: A Group Policy object was created, modified or linked by an account that is not on the approved GPO-admin list. Malicious GPOs were used in 2026 for domain-wide ransomware and extortion (Kaspersky GERT PAYLOAD case).
recommendedActions: Confirm the change with the GPO owner. Review the GPO's settings, scheduled tasks and scripts in SYSVOL. If unauthorized, unlink the GPO, reset the actor's credentials and check for 1b/1c alerts.

displayName: AD Visibility 1b - GPO linked at domain root
description: The gPLink attribute of the domain head object was changed, so a GPO now applies to every computer and user in the domain. Used by the PAYLOAD actor to push encryption tasks domain-wide.
recommendedActions: Treat as urgent. Identify the newly linked GPO, inspect its scheduled tasks/scripts/files, unlink it if not approved and contain the actor account.

displayName: AD Visibility 1c - Executable or task payload written to SYSVOL Policies
description: An executable, script or Group Policy Preferences task/file definition was written under SYSVOL\Policies on a domain controller by an account not on the GPO-admin list.
recommendedActions: Check the file hash and contents, find the GPO GUID in the path and review who changed it. Correlate with AD Visibility 1a/1b alerts.

displayName: AD Visibility 2 - UPN set to another account's sAMAccountName (ResetNightmare)
description: An account's userPrincipalName was set to a bare value (no @suffix) that equals another account's sAMAccountName. This is the setup step for ResetNightmare (CVE-2026-27912), which lets the attacker reset the colliding account's password via kpasswd.
recommendedActions: Revert the UPN, check whether the colliding account's password was reset in the following hour, verify the April 2026 cumulative update is installed on all DCs and review who holds write access to userPrincipalName.

displayName: AD Visibility 3 - Invisible Unicode in UPN/SPN/name (KerberLoss)
description: An identity attribute was written with zero-width or other invisible Unicode characters, a technique used by KerberLoss (CVE-2026-25177) to create look-alike UPNs/SPNs that break Kerberos and force NTLM fallback.
recommendedActions: Inspect the raw attribute value, remove the duplicate/look-alike object and check the NTLM-downgrade tile on the dashboard for affected services.

displayName: AD Visibility 4a - Edge-device service account running new LDAP queries
description: A firewall/VPN LDAP bind account ran queries not seen in its 30-day baseline, or connected from an IP that is not the appliance. Edge-device compromise followed by AD recon with the appliance's own account was seen in 2026 (PAN-OS CVE-2026-0300, Qilin, PAYLOAD).
recommendedActions: Check the appliance for compromise and current advisories, rotate the bind account password and restrict it to the appliance IP and least privilege.

displayName: AD Visibility 4b - Edge-device service account used outside LDAP
description: A firewall/VPN LDAP bind account authenticated with a non-LDAP logon type or from a non-appliance IP, indicating the credential was harvested from the device and reused.
recommendedActions: Disable or rotate the account, investigate the source device and the edge appliance.

displayName: AD Visibility 5 - AD FS DKM container permissions changed (CVE-2026-56155)
description: The security descriptor or owner of the AD FS DKM container (CN=ADFS,CN=Microsoft,CN=Program Data) changed. CVE-2026-56155 (CISA KEV) abuses this ACL to read the token-signing key decryption material, enabling Golden SAML.
recommendedActions: Revert the ACL, check for MDI 'AD FS DKM key read' or 'Golden SAML' alerts within 24h, patch AD FS and consider rolling the token-signing certificate.

displayName: AD Visibility 6 - Computer account created by non-privileged user
description: A standard user created a computer object using ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota. Attacker-owned computer accounts are the first step in RBCD, ResetNightmare and Certighost chains.
recommendedActions: Confirm the computer is legitimate, delete it if not, and set ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota to 0 with delegated join rights instead.

displayName: AD Visibility 7 - Delegation or Kerberos pre-auth setting changed
description: Unconstrained/constrained delegation was configured, or 'Do not require Kerberos pre-authentication' was set, on an account. These changes set up targeted AS-REP roasting or impersonation.
recommendedActions: Verify with the account owner, revert unapproved flags and reset the target account's password if pre-auth was disabled.

displayName: AD Visibility 8 - Change to tier-0-adjacent group
description: An account was added to a tier-0-adjacent group outside the default MDI sensitive-group list (DnsAdmins, Exchange Windows Permissions, ESX/hypervisor/backup admins, etc.) or removed from Protected Users.
recommendedActions: Validate the change request. Consider tagging these groups as sensitive in MDI so built-in alerts also cover them.

displayName: AD Visibility 9 - NTDS.dit extraction activity
description: ntdsutil IFM/snapshot, copying ntds.dit, esentutl /vss, or shadow-copy creation on a domain controller was observed. Called out in the Sep 2026 Five Eyes AD compromise guidance.
recommendedActions: Isolate investigation to the account and host, look for staged .dit/SYSTEM hive files and exfiltration. If confirmed, plan a full credential reset including krbtgt (twice).

displayName: AD Visibility 10 - Trust account authenticated as a user
description: An inter-domain trust account (DOMAIN$) authenticated via Kerberos or NTLM. Five Eyes guidance (Sep 2026) describes obtaining a TGT for the trust account to bypass one-way trusts.
recommendedActions: Baseline legitimate trust traffic first. If unexpected, reset the trust password on both sides and investigate the trusting domain.

displayName: AD Visibility 12 - LAPS or gMSA password read by unapproved account
description: An account outside the approved reader list read LAPS or gMSA password attributes.
recommendedActions: Confirm the reader's role; remove the read permission if not needed.

displayName: AD Sequence 13 - RMM or tunnel on a DC followed by NTDS extraction
description: An RMM or tunnelling tool ran on a domain controller and NTDS.dit or registry-hive extraction followed within 24 hours. Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports this ordering for Storm-2570 (Sep 2026) and Storm-1175 (Apr 2026).
recommendedActions: Isolate the DC from the internet, remove the unsanctioned RMM/tunnel, treat all domain credentials as exposed, and plan a double krbtgt reset.

displayName: AD Sequence 14 - Short-lived scheduled task on a DC ran credential or archive tooling
description: A scheduled task was created on a domain controller, ran ntdsutil/makecab/archive tooling, and was deleted within 15 minutes. Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes this pattern in the Apr 2026 domain-compromise and Mar 2026 high-value-asset posts.
recommendedActions: Identify the remote account that registered the task, look for output archives under Windows\Temp, and treat NTDS as compromised if ntdsutil ran.

displayName: AD Sequence 15 - GPO change followed by payload and trigger in SYSVOL
description: A GPO change was followed within 30 minutes by an executable/script and a ScheduledTasks.xml/Registry.pol/scripts.ini written to the same SYSVOL policy folder. Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes GPO-delivered ransomware in Mar 2026 and Apr 2026 (Storm-1175).
recommendedActions: Unlink the GPO immediately, block the payload hash, and check gPLink at the domain root and OUs.

displayName: AD Sequence 16 - Privileged password reset by another account, then used
description: A privileged or high-criticality account had its password reset by a different, non-approved account and then signed in within 24 hours. Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports this takeover step in the Apr 2026 domain-compromise case.
recommendedActions: Confirm the reset with the account owner and resetter, disable the account if unconfirmed, and review the resetter's other recent activity.

displayName: AD Sequence 17 - Impacket-style remote execution on an Entra Connect server
description: wmiexec/atexec/psexec/smbexec-style execution was observed on an Entra Connect or Cloud Sync server. Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports these servers as targets in the Apr 2026 and Mar 2026 posts.
recommendedActions: Treat as Tier 0: isolate, rotate the AD DS connector and Entra sync accounts, and review Entra sign-ins from the sync identity.

displayName: AD Sequence 18 - Defender tampering on a DC followed by mass deployment
description: Defender settings were weakened on a domain controller and, within 2 hours, the DC launched PsExec with a host list, PDQ, or a forced remote GPUpdate. Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports this staging for Storm-2570 (Sep 2026) and Storm-1175 (Apr 2026).
recommendedActions: Isolate the DC and contain the account immediately; this is typically minutes before encryption.

displayName: AD Sequence 19 - Remote-support session followed by AD recon or WinRM to Tier 0
description: Quick Assist, a silent MSI from PowerShell, or Node.js from AppData ran on a workstation, followed within 4 hours by domain discovery or WinRM to a DC/Tier-0 host. Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports this chain in the Sep 2026 Teams IT-support impersonation campaign.
recommendedActions: Contact the user out of band to confirm the support session, end any Quick Assist sessions, and reset the user's credentials if unconfirmed.
